answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it burns the copper fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the atlas ledger attributes every share, the nebula audit reveals the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 46% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 7 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
